reviews.verdict:
Yes, the planned RQ1-RQ4 paper is one study rather than a set of separate observations, though the arc is not yet closed. Both student drafts are parallel findings. Draft B's sections are "4.1 Balance effects differ across models", "4.2 A balancing benefit survives holdout", "4.3 Selection and budget change the picture" and "4.4 Complementary CausalPFN controls"; they share a theme but no argument, and Draft A ends by saying it does "not establish ... a causal explanation". The planned paper is a chain instead. It holds one model, one dataset, one manipulated variable (the outcome share at fixed K) and one metric (Q-hat), and each RQ asks the question the previous answer raises: RQ1 shows the inversion and its repair, RQ2 asks whose property it is, RQ3 asks what goes with it, and RQ4 asks whether the repair can be tuned and where it stops working. Three seams keep it from a full arc.

1. The explanation step does not explain the remedy. RQ3 lists "при T+Y корреляция около нуля, а Q̂ положителен" as a counterexample, so the paper's headline repair sits outside its own explanation. RQ3 also only describes Do-PFN, so it leaves RQ2's open point ("Почему переворачивается именно Do-PFN, не установлено") unanswered.

2. The dose-response evidence is split between RQ3 (H4, the rho signs) and RQ4 (H3, the 35% dip). RQ4's role also changes with the pending 10-seed result. If 20% beats T+Y, RQ4 becomes a second remedy that competes with RQ1's T+Y headline and with Discussion takeaway 1. If it does not, RQ4 is a clean "limits" step.

3. LZD and the five-dataset material appear as scattered caveats or orphans. The LZD caveats sit in RQ1, RQ3 and RQ4. The "10 из 15" selection statistic and the leak-probe "подводные камни оценки" section belong to no RQ.

With the dose curve moved into RQ3, RQ4 reframed as the limits step and LZD gathered in one place, the abstract reads as one story under either RQ4 outcome.
reviews.central_claim_as_you_read_it: On Criteo, with a fixed-size context, the share of positive outcomes in the context, not the context size, decides whether Do-PFN ranks uplift in the right direction. With random or treatment-balanced contexts it ranks backwards at every K from 512 to 4096. On the 2.09M-row holdout Q-hat is -0.046, and 94-97% of predicted effects are negative while the true ATE is +1.01 pp. Balancing outcomes within each arm (T+Y) flips the sign to +0.048 without retraining (difference +0.094 [0.037; 0.150]). The failure belongs to Do-PFN: CausalPFN, TabPFN-T, a logistic T-learner and a HistGB S-learner on the same 1024 rows do not invert. It coincides with Do-PFN's scores being anti-correlated with baseline risk mu0, which matters on Criteo because uplift sits in the two top risk deciles (2.4 and 4.3 pp). Tuning the share further (20%) helps only partly and does not carry over to LZD.
what_holds_it_together: A single manipulated variable runs through all four RQs: the outcome share in the context at fixed K. RQ1 compares T with T+Y (50%), RQ3 runs the share curve R/T/10/20/35/50/75%, and RQ4 compares 20% with T+Y and 35%. This is the main gain over the drafts, which varied K, the sampler, the dataset, the model and the retrieval method all at once.
The one-line thesis covers three of the four RQs. "состав ... а не его размер" is RQ1, "свойство модели, а не данных" is RQ2, and "чинится составом контекста без переобучения" is RQ1 plus RQ4.

RQ2 follows directly from RQ1. Once composition decides the sign, the obvious objection is "are 1024 rows with about 5% positives simply too few?", and the same-budget control answers it: classical models on the same rows give Q-hat +0.005 to +0.025, and Do-PFN loses to them in 12-14 of 15 paired runs.

The baselines are deliberately paired. Same-budget classical learners on 1024 rows serve attribution in RQ2. Big-data S- and T-learners on 2M rows (Q-hat 0.082 / 0.079) serve competitiveness in RQ4. Stating this pairing explicitly gives the paper a visible spine.

Predictions set from CV were checked on held-out data. H2 (20% beats T, +0.128 [+0.091, +0.168]) and H3 (the 35% dip, -0.082 [-0.110, -0.055], 3 of 3 seeds) replicated. For H4, rho(score, mu0) had the predicted sign at 20%, T and 35% in every seed, but the protocol's bootstrap condition was not computed, so it is "Not formally replicated". This is the strongest connection between CV and the holdout in the project.

The problem statement is vivid and concrete. With context T the mean CATE is -5.4 / -9.6 / -8.0 pp against a true ATE of +1.01 pp (review section 4.1), so the reader sees the inversion as a wrong-signed effect, not just a low Qini.

The "Чего в статье не утверждаем" list bounds the story consistently. It rules out generalising to all causal FMs, calls T+Y case-control rather than a new method, calls the holdout check internally specified rather than pre-registered, rules out a mechanism claim and drops Feature-kNN, which removes the drafts' biggest orphan.
what_feels_disconnected: RQ3 does not explain RQ1's remedy. At T+Y, rho(score, mu0) is about 0 (CV +0.03, holdout -0.12 / -0.03 / +0.08), yet Q-hat is positive, and RQ3 lists this under "Контрпримеры". The abstract would say "T+Y repairs it" and then "the sign tracks risk alignment", and a reader will ask why T+Y works when it does not flip that alignment.

RQ3 does not answer the question RQ2 leaves open. RQ2's status says "Почему переворачивается именно Do-PFN, не установлено", but RQ3 reports rho(score, mu0) for Do-PFN only. Without the same statistic for CausalPFN, TabPFN-T or the logistic T-learner on the same contexts, RQ3 describes Do-PFN's failure without contrasting it with the models that do not fail. RQ3 then reads as a side observation, not as the next step after RQ2.

The thesis "Это свойство модели, а не данных" conflicts with two pieces of evidence the paper itself contains. First, RQ3 shows that "Истинный uplift на Criteo сосредоточен в двух верхних децилях риска". That is a property of the data, and it is what makes anti-alignment with risk so damaging; LZD, where "связь с Q̂ не прослеживается", is consistent with this. Second, review section 4.3 says "Часть эффекта доли — общая": the logistic T-learner improves from 0.016 to 0.057 at 20%, and 75% hurts every model. RQ2's answer leaves out this generic part, so RQ4's dose result looks more Do-PFN-specific than it is.

The dose-response evidence is split across two RQs. H4 (the rho signs) is used in RQ3, H3 (the 35% dip) in RQ4, and the review's suggested central figure (Q-hat and rho against the share of Y=1) serves both. RQ3 also says "При лучшей доле 20%", which assumes the RQ4 result that is still pending.

RQ4's place in the arc depends on the outcome. (a) If the 10-seed check confirms 20% > T+Y, RQ4 becomes a second, better remedy. It then competes with RQ1's headline and contradicts Discussion takeaway 1 ("балансировать исходы внутри групп", which means 50%), while the 20% optimum does not transfer to LZD ("на LZD доля 20% хуже T+Y (CV −0,026)"). (b) If it is not confirmed, RQ4 cleanly closes the arc as the limits step.

RQ1 asks two questions joined by "and": does composition decide the sign, and does the repair hold on the holdout. The remedy therefore appears before the explanation, so the order is problem plus remedy, then attribution, then association, then tuning, not problem, explanation, remedy, limits. The "rather than its size" half also has no number in RQ1's tables, which are for K = 1024 only.

LZD is scattered as a caveat in RQ1 ("LZD повторяет знаки только в пределах шума"), RQ3 and RQ4. Meanwhile the LZD finding that would help RQ2 is unused: review section 4.4 reports the same non-monotone rho sign pattern on LZD, positive at 20% in 15 of 15 runs and mostly negative at 35%, and concludes "Это указывает на свойство модели, а не датасета".

Orphan: Discussion takeaway 2 ("10 из 15 выбранных по CV конфигураций хуже на холдауте", and TabPFN-T falling from 0.077 to 0.006). It comes from the five-dataset selection study in Draft B section 4.3, which lies outside the "Criteo Case Study" scope and answers no RQ.
Orphan: the "раздел про подводные камни оценки" planned around the leak probe (the `leak` job). It is a fifth thread with no RQ behind it.

Orphan: Hillstrom, Orange and RetailHero, the three datasets that are neither Criteo nor LZD, disappear without a sentence, although the drafts' Table 1/2 covers all five datasets. A reviewer who has seen the abstract style of the drafts will ask where they went.

The calibration point is split. The scale problem appears in RQ1 (94-97% negative) and again in RQ4 ("средний предсказанный эффект +6…+7 п.п. при истинном +1,0 п.п."), where it reads as a side remark rather than a limit.
fixes: Rewrite RQ3 as three states of alignment rather than as an association with counterexamples. Anti-aligned: R, T, 10% and 35% (rho(score, mu0) about -0.5 to -0.7, rho(score, uplift) about -0.16 to -0.33). Neutralised: T+Y (rho with mu0 about 0, rho with uplift +0.12, 15/15). Aligned: 20% (+0.47 / +0.33, 15/15). The T+Y repair then becomes part of the explanation, "balancing removes the wrong-signed risk component", and only 35% on CV (Q-hat +0.021 with rho -0.46) remains a named counterexample. On the holdout, 35% is consistent (Q-hat about -0.007).

Add a comparison row or column to RQ3: rho(score, mu0) at R/T for CausalPFN, TabPFN-T and the logistic T-learner on the same CV contexts. This is a CPU computation from the existing mechanism_runs.csv, and it turns RQ3 into the direct answer to RQ2's "why Do-PFN?".

Reword the thesis from "свойство модели, а не данных" to a model x data statement. Do-PFN's scores track baseline risk with a sign set by the outcome share; on Criteo, where uplift is concentrated in the top risk deciles, that sign decides the ranking. To check whether LZD's non-transfer is predicted rather than accidental, compute an uplift-by-mu0-decile table on LZD (CPU, minutes).

In RQ2's answer, split the T+Y effect into the Do-PFN-specific sign repair and a generic case-control efficiency gain: logistic T from 0.016 to 0.057 at 20%, and 75% hurting all models (review section 4.3). This links RQ2 to the case-control positioning in "Чего не утверждаем" and prepares RQ4.

Move the share curve (Q-hat and rho against share, with T, T+Y and the logistic control) into RQ3 as the main figure, and present H3 (the 35% dip, -0.082 [-0.107; -0.058]) and H4 (rho signs) as out-of-sample tests of RQ3. Narrow RQ4 to "Is tuning the share worth it beyond balancing?": 20% vs T+Y over 10 seeds, 20% vs the 2M-row S/T-learners (S minus 20% = +0.007 [-0.006; +0.020]), LZD transfer, and calibration.

Write both versions of RQ4 and of the abstract sentence now, and keep T+Y as the headline remedy in either case. (a) "A CV-tuned 20% share adds a further +0.024 Q-hat [two-level CI] and matches 2M-row learners, but the optimum is dataset-specific (LZD favours 50%)." (b) "Beyond balancing, tuning the share is not reliable: 20% vs T+Y lies within context-to-context variation and reverses on LZD." In version (a), describe 20% as evidence that the alignment can be steered, not as a recommended setting.

Gather LZD into one "Transfer" paragraph that ends RQ4 as the limits step. What replicates: negative Q-hat at R and T (-0.016 to -0.017), and the rho sign pattern at 20% and 35%. What does not: the optimum share (50%), the link to Q-hat, and competitiveness (FMs at most 0.016 vs a T-learner at 0.051). Use the replicating sign pattern as supporting evidence in RQ2.

Split RQ1 into its problem half (inversion at every K from 512 to 4096; 94-97% negative effects; mean CATE -5.4 to -9.6 pp) and its repair half. Add one line of Q-hat at T for K = 512/2048/4096 to support "rather than its size". Put the calibration point here, not in RQ4.

Add one sentence in the Setup on why the paper studies Criteo only, using the drafts' CV deltas for Do-PFN T+Y minus T: Hillstrom +0.012, LZD +0.035, Orange -0.002, RetailHero -0.010. This closes the gap left by the three datasets that are otherwise silently dropped.
Make the paired-baseline spine explicit in the text: same-budget learners for attribution (RQ2) and big-data learners for competitiveness (RQ4).
Change "при лучшей доле 20%" in RQ3 to "при доле 20%", and avoid "frozen holdout" in RQ1, given that "Холдаут ранее уже использовался".
what_to_cut: Both drafts' retrieval and Feature-kNN material: Draft A's "Complementary query-dependent retrieval" paragraph and its abstract sentence "An independent exploratory study of query-dependent context selection..."; Draft B section 4.4 (E17 -0.117 pp, E19 LZD cell +1.429 pp, runtime 17.0 to 76.3 min); and Draft B's abstract sentence "Complementary CausalPFN retrieval controls further limit attribution...". These are the drafts' clearest orphans.
The five-dataset tables (Draft A Table 1, Draft B Tables 2 and 3) as results. Reduce them to the single Setup sentence that justifies the Criteo focus.

Discussion takeaway 2's "10 из 15 выбранных по CV конфигураций хуже на холдауте", which is a five-dataset selection statistic. Keep only the Criteo part, the seed SD of 0.041-0.047 for CausalPFN and TabPFN-T and TabPFN-T's drop from 0.077 to 0.006, as a caveat to RQ2's cross-model comparison.
The planned "раздел про подводные камни оценки" built around the leak probe. At most one Setup sentence on grouping identical feature vectors, with the rest in the repository.

Draft B section 4.1's paragraph "Larger contexts are not uniformly preferable" on CausalPFN and TabPFN-T size effects (+0.01353 / -0.00757). The only size evidence the paper needs is Do-PFN inverting at every K.
Draft B section 4.3's Hillstrom uplift@10% comparison of TabPFN-T and Do-PFN (10.264 vs 9.195 pp).
The duplicated calibration remark in RQ4 ("+6…+7 п.п."). State it once, as a limit.

reviews.verdict:
Yes. The planned RQ1-RQ4 paper reads as one argument, not a collection of observations, and it is a clear step up from drafts A and B. Both drafts are descriptive grids with a retrieval side-study attached, and both say so: A writes "they do not establish a universal best sampler or a causal explanation", and B writes "We do not ... establish a causal explanation for backbone differences". The planned paper has one manipulated variable (the outcome share of a fixed-size context), one model (Do-PFN), one dataset (Criteo) and one primary metric (Q-hat), and RQ1 -> RQ2 -> RQ3 follows a natural order: phenomenon, then where it sits, then what it looks like.

The evidence chain is strongest at the first link and weakens after it. RQ1's holdout repair is solid: Q-hat goes from -0.046 to +0.048, a gain of +0.094 with t-interval [0.037; 0.150] over three contexts. RQ2, which says the inversion belongs to the model, rests on CV and Criteo only. RQ3 is an association that is close to mechanical on Criteo. RQ4 is a practical tuning question whose role in the paper changes with the result of the 10-seed run.

Two clauses of the one-line thesis go beyond what the RQs establish:
- "rather than its size" is supported only by CV over K 512-4096, has no table or figure in the plan, and the review recommends cutting the size paragraph.
- "это свойство модели, а не данных" (it is a property of the model, not the data) is not shown. RQ2 separates the model from the context rows, not from the dataset, and only one dataset is reliable.

The Discussion also draws on evidence that no RQ sets up: the five-dataset "10 из 15" (10 of 15) selection statistic, and a general "балансировать исходы" (balance the outcomes) rule for binary outcomes. "Что осталось до подачи" (what remains before submission) plans a leak probe for a "раздел про подводные камни оценки" (section on evaluation pitfalls) that no RQ needs.

If the thesis is narrowed, RQ2 gets a holdout version (cheap, CPU only), RQ3 and RQ4 are merged around the share curve, and the leftover draft material is cut, the paper holds together under either outcome of the 10-seed check.
reviews.central_claim_as_you_read_it: On Criteo, the share of Y=1 within each treatment arm of a fixed-size context (K=1024; CV across K 512-4096) decides whether Do-PFN ranks uplift in the right direction or backwards. Under random (R) and treatment-balanced (T) contexts the ranking is inverted: holdout Q-hat is -0.046, and 94-97% of predicted effects are negative while the ATE is +1.01 pp. The inversion belongs to Do-PFN, not to the rows it reads: CausalPFN, TabPFN-T, a logistic T-learner and a HistGB S-learner given the same rows do not invert. It goes together with Do-PFN's scores being anti-aligned with baseline risk mu0, and the sign of that alignment follows the outcome share. Rebalancing outcomes (T+Y, and possibly a tuned 20% share) repairs the inversion without retraining: holdout Q-hat rises by +0.094 [0.037; 0.150]. The repair applies to ranking only, not to CATE estimates.
what_holds_it_together: The paper has a single manipulated variable, and it is an intervention on the context, so causal wording about 'composition decides the sign' is justified for Do-PFN on Criteo. Every RQ varies the outcome share of the same K=1024 context and reads the same metric (Q-hat). This is the basic difference from drafts A and B, whose variables were 5 datasets x 3 models x 4 K x 3 strategies (A: 'Across five datasets, four context budgets, and three sampling schemes').

RQ1's main link holds out of sample, and in the right unit. CV gives T+Y > T in 15 of 15 runs and 5 of 5 folds (Wilcoxon p = 6e-5). On the holdout, the +0.094 gain has t-interval [0.037; 0.150] over three contexts. holdout_share_protocol.md shows that 'For Do-PFN the run seed changes only the context', so a t-interval over seeds is the correct uncertainty over contexts, unlike the drafts' bootstrap [0.0849, 0.1024], which holds contexts fixed.

RQ2 turns draft A's descriptive transfer contrast I(a,b) = Delta_a - Delta_b into a tested localization claim: Do-PFN gains more from T+Y than CausalPFN (+0.13 [0.04; 0.21]) and than TabPFN-T (+0.14 [0.06; 0.22]). The same-rows classical controls answer the obvious objection 'is it just a small sample?': logistic T-learner and HistGB S-learner reach Q-hat +0.005 to +0.025, and Do-PFN loses to them in 12-14 of 15 paired runs.

RQ3 links the sign of the ranking to a measurable property of the scores, and that sign pattern replicates on the holdout in every seed. holdout_share_protocol.md gives rho(score, mu0) of +0.20/+0.64/+0.22 at 20%, -0.34/-0.62/-0.50 at T, and -0.57/-0.46/-0.36 at 35%. It also lists its own counterexamples (T+Y has rho near 0 with Q-hat > 0; 35% on CV has rho < 0 with Q-hat > 0; no link on LZD) instead of hiding them.

RQ4 contributes the strongest out-of-sample evidence that composition matters as a continuous variable, not merely 'balanced vs not'. The 35% dip replicates (35% - 20% = -0.082, t-interval [-0.107; -0.058], 3 of 3 seeds), and 20% - T = +0.128 [+0.091, +0.168]. Both were specified in an internal protocol, with a decision rule, before the results were available.

The 'Чего в статье не утверждаем' list (what the paper does not claim) mostly matches the evidence: no claim to cover all causal FMs, T+Y is not presented as a new method (positioned against Nyberg et al. and McDowell et al. 2026), the protocol is not called pre-registered, RQ3 is not called a mechanism, and Feature-kNN is not claimed to help (E17 -0.165 pp [-0.699; +0.409]). The working title 'A Criteo Case Study' is honest about scope.
what_feels_disconnected: The thesis clause 'а не его размер' (rather than its size) and the 'rather than its size' wording in RQ1's title have only CV support and no display item. The RQ1 answer says Do-PFN inverts 'при любом K от 512 до 4096' (at any K from 512 to 4096), but the planned tables are 'таблица 1 (CV, K = 1024) и таблица 2 (холдаут)' (Table 1 CV at K = 1024, Table 2 holdout), and the holdout has K=1024 only. Meanwhile review section 7 says 'Что сократить ради места: Абзац про размер контекста' (cut the context-size paragraph to save space). The plan therefore keeps a claim in the thesis while cutting its evidence.

'Это свойство модели, а не данных' (a property of the model, not the data) is not what RQ2 tests. RQ2's title asks whether the inversion is 'a property of the context rows or of the model that reads them'. With 'надёжный датасет один' (one reliable dataset), and LZD repeating the signs only 'в пределах шума' (within noise: Q-hat -0.016 to -0.017 at an SD of 0.02-0.03), the paper cannot separate a Do-PFN property from a Do-PFN x Criteo interaction.

The chain moves from holdout evidence (RQ1) to CV-only evidence (RQ2) at the step the thesis depends on most. RQ2 status says 'Только CV и только Criteo' (CV only, Criteo only). On the holdout, CausalPFN and TabPFN-T were scored only at their CV-selected 4096/T configurations: 0.00311 +/- 0.04134 and 0.00676 +/- 0.04644 (draft B, Table 3). Those are neither inverted nor distinguishable from zero, and they use a different K and a different context from Do-PFN's 1024/T. No classical same-row control was run on the holdout contexts.

RQ3 is close to a restatement of RQ1 in different coordinates, so it cannot answer RQ2's open question ('Почему переворачивается именно Do-PFN, не установлено', why it is Do-PFN specifically that inverts is not established). On Criteo, observed uplift sits in the top two mu0 deciles (2.4 and 4.3 pp, against about 0 in deciles 1-7), and a good ranker aligns with mu0: the reference S-learner has tau vs mu0 = +0.79 in the holdout file. Any score anti-aligned with mu0 must therefore have a negative Qini. The association is also one-directional: Q-hat < 0 implies rho < 0, but 35% on CV has rho(score, mu0) = -0.46 (0/15) while Q-hat = +0.021 (12/15), and in the review's table rho(score, uplift) = -0.16 (0/15) at the same point. Review section 4.2 still says 'Q̂ следует за знаком связи с uplift' (Q-hat follows the sign of the link with uplift) and 'Провал при 35% ... объясняется тем же переворотом' (the dip at 35% is explained by the same reversal); that wording contradicts its own table and must not reach the paper.

RQ4 asks a different kind of question ('tuned ... into a reliable, competitive ranker'), so its answer reshapes the story instead of extending it. With the current 3 seeds, 20% vs T+Y gains +0.024 with t-interval [-0.003; +0.052], i.e. 'в пределах разброса между контекстами' (within the spread between contexts). 'Reliable' is contradicted by LZD (20% worse than T+Y, CV -0.026). 'Competitive' compares against S- and T-learners fitted on 2M development rows (0.082 / 0.079), while RQ2's fair comparison uses learners with the same 1024-row budget. If the 10-seed run confirms 20% > T+Y, the paper's repair turns into a CV-tuned hyperparameter that does not transfer, and the thesis sentence (T+Y repairs) and the headline result (20% is best) pull apart. If it does not confirm, the 'competitive ranker' part has no support: T+Y on the 200k rows is 0.051 against S 0.082.

Discussion point 1 ('балансировать исходы внутри групп контекста', balance outcomes within context groups, for any binary outcome) goes beyond every RQ. The five-dataset CV table in both drafts shows T+Y hurting Do-PFN on RetailHero (-0.0104) and Orange (-0.0021), and the RQ file itself says generalizing to 'rare outcomes' in general is not allowed.

Discussion point 2 ('10 из 15 выбранных по CV конфигураций хуже на холдауте', 10 of 15 CV-selected configurations are worse on the holdout; the CV leader TabPFN-T falls from 0.077 to 0.006) depends on the five-dataset, 12-configuration selection protocol, which no RQ introduces. Draft B section 4.3 also notes that this drop is not purely selection: 'The full holdout and limited CV evaluation sets also differ in size and composition'.

'Что осталось до подачи' (what remains before submission) plans a duplicate-leak probe on 5 seeds for a 'раздел про подводные камни оценки' (section on evaluation pitfalls). That section is a second theme (fragile FM evaluation) that competes with the Do-PFN composition thesis for space in 4 pages, and no RQ needs it.

Several load-bearing numbers have no file behind them yet. The plan says the RQ2 interaction test, the RQ3 mu0-decile uplift table, the rho bootstrap and the paired bootstrap against the references exist 'часть пока только в выводе агентов' (partly only in agent output). H4 is 'Not formally replicated' because the bootstrap for rho was not computed.

The holdout's history weakens the word 'frozen' beyond RQ1. holdout_share_protocol.md: 'The holdout is not untouched. It was scored in the 48 frozen runs, and the CV mechanism probe fitted its Criteo reference on holdout rows.' RQ1's T-vs-T+Y contrast was fixed before its holdout results were inspected, but RQ4 and the RQ3 holdout signs come from a holdout that had already been used.

Both drafts list a confound that the plan never addresses: the preprocessing is fitted on the selected context. Draft B: 'a strategy changes both selected examples and preprocessing estimates'. Draft A: 'The improvement could reflect ... context-dependent preprocessing'. RQ1's 'composition decides' therefore silently includes the preprocessing step.
fixes: Rewrite the one-line thesis to match what the RQs test. For example: 'On Criteo, the outcome share of a fixed-size context (K = 512-4096) decides the sign of Do-PFN's uplift ranking. Two other PFNs and classical learners given the same rows do not invert, so the inversion lies in how Do-PFN reads the context, not in the rows, and rebalancing the context repairs it without retraining.' Replace 'свойство модели, а не данных' (model, not data) with 'model, not context rows'. Mention the K range in the abstract and justify it as budget-constrained, because reviewers will contrast it with CausalPFN's ~40k contexts.

Give RQ2 a holdout leg; this needs CPU only. Fit the logistic T-learner and the HistGB S-learner on the exact three frozen holdout contexts (T and T+Y, seeds 42-44, K=1024) and score them on the same holdout rows or the 200k subsample. This closes the CV-only gap between RQ1 and RQ2 at the point where the thesis needs it. If CausalPFN and TabPFN-T at K=1024 T/T+Y were never scored on the holdout, say explicitly that the cross-FM part of RQ2 is CV only.

Either support 'rather than its size' or remove it. To support it, add one small panel of Do-PFN CV Q-hat against K (512, 1024, 2048, 4096) for R, T and T+Y, and cut only the CausalPFN/TabPFN-T size results that the review marked for cutting (draft B 4.1: +0.01353 / -0.00757 / +0.03586 / +0.00575). Otherwise, drop the clause from the RQ1 title and the thesis.

reviews.verdict:
Yes. The planned RQ1-RQ4 version reads as a focused contribution, not a collection of observations, if two conditions are met. RQ1, RQ2 and RQ3 form one chain about one model (Do-PFN), one knob (the outcome share in a fixed-size context), one metric (Q-hat) and one dataset (Criteo). RQ1 is the phenomenon: an inverted ranking that T+Y repairs on the 2.09M-row holdout, Q-hat -0.046 -> +0.048, difference +0.094, t-interval [0.037; 0.150]. RQ2 is the attribution: on the same 1,024 rows, CausalPFN, TabPFN-T, a logistic T-learner and a HistGB S-learner do not invert, and the interaction is +0.13 [0.04; 0.21] and +0.14 [0.06; 0.22]. RQ3 is the correlate: every inverted run has rho(score, mu0) < 0. Each RQ answers the obvious objection to the one before it. A skeptical WSDM reviewer can sum this up in one sentence, and that is the test.

Two things could still push it back toward 'a set of observations':
(1) RQ4 as now worded ('tuned on cross-validation into a reliable, competitive ranker'). This is a benchmarking question. Its headline contrast, 20% - T+Y with a t-interval of [-0.003; +0.052], may come out null in the 10-seed run, and the 20% optimum does not carry over to LZD (CV -0.026).
(2) Leftovers from draft B: the CV-selection degradation (10 of 15), TabPFN-T falling from 0.077 to 0.006, the leak-probe 'pitfalls' section, the size paragraph, and the retrieval pilot with E17 and E19.

The student drafts as written would score about 4. Both end on 'it depends' conclusions. B's own conclusion reads: 'Context balance has model- and dataset-dependent empirical effects on uplift ranking.' Both also attach retrieval experiments that use a different model and a different protocol.

The summary sentence I would put in the review: 'On Criteo, the released Do-PFN checkpoint ranks uplift in the wrong direction whenever its 1,024-row context keeps the natural ~4-5% outcome rate; balancing outcomes within each treatment arm reverses the sign on a 2.09M-row holdout (normalized Qini -0.046 -> +0.048), whereas CausalPFN, a TabPFN T-learner and classical learners fitted on the same rows do not invert, and every inverted run coincides with Do-PFN scores anti-correlated with baseline risk.'

I would score it as coherent if three things hold: every table and figure answers one RQ; RQ4 is recast so the paper stays correct under both outcomes of the 10-seed run; and the thesis is worded only as strongly as the evidence (Criteo only, an association rather than a mechanism).

Coherence is a separate question from significance. The objection most likely to remain is narrowness, not fragmentation: one checkpoint, used outside its stated continuous-outcome regime, and one reliable dataset.

Sources: <project>/paper_RQ_2026-11-09.md, <project>/review_student_drafts_2026-11-09.md, <project>/repro/holdout_share_protocol.md, and the two draft texts a.txt and b.txt.
reviews.central_claim_as_you_read_it:
The central claim has four parts:
- In a fixed-size context (K = 512-4096), the share of positive outcomes, not the number of rows, decides whether Do-PFN ranks Criteo uplift in the right direction. With random or treatment-balanced contexts it ranks in reverse: holdout Q-hat is -0.046, and 94-97% of predicted effects are negative while the true ATE is +1.01 pp.
- Within-arm outcome balancing (T+Y) repairs the sign without retraining: holdout Q-hat +0.048, difference +0.094 [0.037; 0.150].
- The failure belongs to Do-PFN reading the rows, not to the rows themselves: two other PFNs and two classical learners fitted on the same 1,024 rows do not invert.
- Inverted runs coincide with scores anti-aligned with baseline risk mu0. On Criteo this matters because true uplift sits in the top two risk deciles (2.4 and 4.3 pp, against about 0 in deciles 1-7).

One tension: the file's one-line thesis says 'Это свойство модели, а не данных'. That reads as a claim of generality across datasets, which a paper titled '...A Criteo Case Study', with 'надёжный датасет один', cannot carry. What RQ2 actually supports is narrower: a property of the model reading the context, not of the context rows.
what_holds_it_together: The scope is tight and consistent: one model, one knob (outcome share), one metric (Q-hat), one reliable dataset. The title 'Outcome Composition Can Invert Do-PFN's Uplift Ranking: A Criteo Case Study' matches the RQs, and the 'Обобщать до causal foundation models ... нельзя' line keeps the scope honest.

RQ1 -> RQ2 -> RQ3 is a classic sequence: phenomenon, then attribution, then correlate. Each RQ answers the skeptic's next question. The review's reviewer-Q table ('Это не просто малая выборка в контексте?') is answered directly by RQ2.

The same-row control ladder in RQ2 turns the drafts' observation ('T+Y helps Do-PFN on Criteo') into a claim about the model. On the same rows the classical learners get Q-hat +0.005 to +0.025, Do-PFN loses 12-14 of 15 paired runs, and the interaction is +0.13 [0.04; 0.21] vs CausalPFN and +0.14 [0.06; 0.22] vs TabPFN-T.

CausalPFN and TabPFN-T are recast from 'three subjects of a grid' (drafts A and B) into controls. TabPFN-T not benefiting from T+Y also gives a positioning contrast with McDowell et al. 2026, where downsampling helps PFN classifiers.

The share sweep (R, T, 10, 20, 35, 50, 75%) links RQ1, RQ3 and RQ4. The sign of rho(score, mu0) flips non-monotonically and Q-hat follows it. The 35% dip predicted on CV replicated out of sample (35% - 20% = -0.082 [-0.107; -0.058], 3 of 3 seeds). That was a falsifiable prediction, and it held.

The wrong sign and the implausible scale tell the same story. Under T the mean CATE is -5.4/-9.6/-8.0 pp with SD 45-71 pp; under T+Y it is +0.7 to +1.7 pp. Discussion takeaway 3 ('only for ranking, not as effect estimates') follows from this.

The 'Чего в статье не утверждаем' list keeps the claims within the evidence: not pre-registered, T+Y is not a new method, the risk link is not a mechanism, and there is no Feature-kNN claim. This reads as one argument, not a set of loosely held findings.
what_feels_disconnected: RQ4 changes the question from diagnosis to benchmarking ('tuned on cross-validation into a reliable, competitive ranker'). Its key numbers are weak: 20% - T+Y = +0.024 with t-interval [-0.003; +0.052]; LZD 20% worse than T+Y (CV -0.026); 'S минус 20% = +0.007 [-0.006; +0.020], условно на контекстах'. If the 10-seed run is null, the paper's last RQ ends on 'partially/no'.

RQ3 explains the failure, not the repair. T+Y works with rho(score, mu0) close to zero (holdout -0.12/-0.03/+0.08). At 35% on CV, rho is -0.46 and yet Q-hat is +0.021. So the link from RQ1's 'repair' to RQ3's 'risk alignment' runs in one direction only, and a reviewer will ask what T+Y actually changes.

Discussion takeaway 2 ('Оценивать конфигурации FM по нескольким контекстам ... TabPFN-T упал с 0,077 до 0,006. 10 из 15 ... хуже на холдауте') and the leak probe planned for a 'раздел про подводные камни оценки' carry a second message about evaluating FMs in general, inherited from draft B section 4.3. They are not about Do-PFN's inversion.

LZD plays three unannounced roles: an RQ1 caveat ('LZD повторяет знаки только в пределах шума'), an RQ3 counterexample ('на LZD связь с Q-hat не прослеживается') and RQ4 counter-evidence (20% worse). The reader cannot tell whether LZD is meant as a replication or as a boundary.
The thesis wording 'свойство модели, а не данных' sits uneasily with the subtitle 'A Criteo Case Study' and with 'надёжный датасет один'.

The 'rather than its size' half of RQ1 is a second sub-claim resting on one clause (inverted at every K from 512 to 4096, CV only). It invites the K <= 4096 vs ~40k (CausalPFN paper) objection without adding to the argument.

The same T+Y configuration has two holdout numbers: 0.048 on the full 2.09M rows (RQ1) and 0.051 on the 200k subsample (RQ4). T is -0.046 vs about -0.053. Unless this is explained, it looks like an inconsistency.

If carried over from the drafts, these read as a collection: the five-dataset tables (A Table 1, B Table 2), B Table 3 (15 selected configs), the size paragraph in B 4.1, the retrieval pilot (A 'Complementary query-dependent retrieval'; B 4.4 with E17, E19 and 'about 17.0 to 76.3 minutes'), and Hillstrom uplift@10% 10.264 vs 9.195.

For example: 'On Criteo, the outcome share of a fixed-size context sets the sign of the released Do-PFN checkpoint's uplift ranking; the inversion belongs to the model reading the context (two other PFNs and classical learners on the same rows do not invert), is repaired by within-arm outcome balancing without retraining, and coincides with Do-PFN scores anti-aligned with baseline risk.' The primary evidence becomes H3 (35% dip, -0.082 [-0.107; -0.058]) and H4 (the sign of rho at T, 20% and 35%, after computing the bootstrap interval for rho, which is a few CPU minutes and already on the to-do list). The 20% vs T+Y contrast drops to one secondary, practical sentence.

Pre-write both RQ4 endings. (A) If the two-level interval excludes zero: 'the CV-tuned share beats T+Y on holdout and reaches the range of big-data S/T learners (0.082/0.079), but the optimum is dataset-specific (LZD prefers 50%)'. But negative alignment does not guarantee failure (35% on CV), and T+Y repairs the ranking with rho close to zero. Say outright that 20% and T+Y appear to repair through different routes, which the per-arm (y1, y0) predictions on GPU would settle.

Move the regime caveat into the introduction: Do-PFN's stated regime is continuous outcomes, and this is the released checkpoint on a standard binary benchmark. Frame the contribution as diagnosis plus a cheap repair for a public causal FM. Position it against McDowell et al. 2026 and against case-control sampling (Prentice-Pyke, King-Zeng, Fithian-Hastie): what is new is the sign inversion in a causal PFN, not the sampler.

Fold the CV-selection and seed-variance evidence into one sentence inside RQ2. It explains why the CausalPFN and TabPFN-T comparisons use intervals over several contexts (holdout SD 0.041-0.047). Drop it as a standalone takeaway.

They use a different model, a different protocol and answer a different question.

synthesis.verdict:
Yes. The planned paper reads as one argument, not a set of separate observations. Score: 7/10. All three reviewers gave 7 independently, and the student drafts as written would score about 4. The plan holds one model (the released Do-PFN checkpoint), one dataset (Criteo), one manipulated variable (the Y=1 share of a fixed K=1024 context) and one metric (Q-hat). Each RQ answers the objection raised by the one before it: RQ1 shows the inversion and that changing the share reverses it, RQ2 asks whose property the inversion is, and RQ3 asks what it goes with. The drafts describe a 5-dataset x 3-model x 4-K x 3-sampler grid, and they say so themselves: B writes "Context balance has model- and dataset-dependent empirical effects", and both write that they do not establish "a causal explanation".

Three seams keep the score from 8-9, and they should be closed before writing:
(1) The one-line thesis says more than the RQs show. "Это свойство модели, а не данных" is not what RQ2 tests. RQ2 separates the model from the context rows, on CV and Criteo only, with "надёжный датасет один". "А не его размер" has no table or figure in the plan, which lists only Table 1 at K=1024 and Table 2 on the holdout, while review section 7 proposes cutting the size paragraph.
(2) RQ3 explains the failure but not the repair. At T+Y, rho(score, mu0) is about 0 (CV +0.03; holdout -0.12/-0.03/+0.08), and the plan lists this under "Контрпримеры". RQ3 also reports rho for Do-PFN only, so it does not answer RQ2's open point, "Почему переворачивается именно Do-PFN, не установлено".
(3) RQ4, worded as "reliable, competitive ranker", asks a benchmarking question, and its role changes with the pending 10-seed run: 20% - T+Y = +0.024 with t-interval [-0.003; +0.052], and LZD 20% - T+Y = -0.026 on CV. Several pieces belong to no RQ: Discussion takeaway 2 ("10 из 15"), the leak-probe "раздел про подводные камни оценки", and the retrieval and Feature-kNN material from both drafts.

The fixes: narrow the thesis, move the share curve and the out-of-sample tests H2-H4 into RQ3, recast RQ4 as a short limits step written to hold under either 10-seed outcome, and cut the orphans. The paper then reads as one story. One reviewer error should not reach the paper. The claim that "75% hurts every model" is wrong. On CV, 75% hurts the same-row classical learners (-0.004 / -0.006), but Do-PFN at 75% has Q-hat +0.066 (14/15). The objection likely to remain is narrowness, not fragmentation: one checkpoint used outside its stated continuous-outcome regime, and one reliable dataset.
synthesis.storyline: In-context causal foundation models are attractive for uplift ranking under a fixed context budget, but which rows enter the context is a modelling choice; we study it for the released Do-PFN checkpoint on Criteo. With random or treatment-balanced contexts (K = 512-4,096 on cross-validation; K = 1,024 on a 2.09M-row holdout), Do-PFN ranks uplift backwards: holdout normalized Qini is -0.046, and 94-97% of predicted effects are negative while the true ATE is +1.01 pp. Changing only the outcome share, by balancing outcomes within each treatment arm, reverses the sign without retraining (Qini +0.048, difference +0.094 [0.037; 0.150] over three contexts). The inversion lies in how Do-PFN reads the context, not in the rows: CausalPFN, a TabPFN T-learner, and logistic and gradient-boosted learners fitted on the same 1,024 rows do not invert, and Do-PFN gains 0.13-0.14 more from balancing than the other two PFNs. Across a sweep of the outcome share, the sign of the ranking goes together with the sign of the correlation between Do-PFN's scores and baseline risk, which decides the ranking on Criteo because observed uplift sits in the top two risk deciles; the non-monotone response predicted on cross-validation, including a dip at 35%, replicates on the holdout. The repair applies to ranking only, not to effect estimates, and the best share is dataset-specific (it does not transfer to LZD), so the practical advice is to check the sign of Do-PFN's ranking on held-out data before trusting it, not to adopt a fixed sampling rule.

synthesis.contribution_sentence: We show, on Criteo, that the outcome share of a fixed-size context sets the sign of the released Do-PFN checkpoint's uplift ranking: the inversion belongs to how Do-PFN reads the context rather than to the rows (other PFNs and classical learners on the same 1,024 rows do not invert), coincides with Do-PFN scores anti-aligned with baseline risk, and is reversed without retraining by balancing outcomes within each treatment arm (holdout normalized Qini -0.046 -> +0.048).
